issue.title: 4.1: Lazy-load graph, map, and table views
issue.body_excerpt: React.lazy the four visualization components from App.jsx.

affected_files.role: primary - convert the four static imports of RadialGraph/BipartiteGraph/MapView/DataTable to React.lazy(); wrap each in <Suspense>; define a Loading fallback. ScreenshotModal.jsx also imports html2canvas and is only mounted on user action, so it can stay static or be lazy.
imports d3 (static). No code change needed; module is the split chunk target.
imports d3 (static). No code change needed; module is the split chunk target.
imports leaflet, leaflet.markercluster, leaflet css (static). No code change needed; module is the split chunk target.
no heavy imports, but lazy-loaded together with the other views for uniform code-splitting.

analysis.current_implementation: App.jsx (lines 17-20) statically imports RadialGraph, BipartiteGraph, MapView, and DataTable. These transitive imports pull in d3, leaflet, leaflet.markercluster, and (via ScreenshotModal) html2canvas into the initial dashboard bundle. The empty-state branch and loading branch do not need any of them.
analysis.limitations: Initial dashboard load pays for ~600KB+ of d3/leaflet that won't be touched unless the user switches to graph/map. With the issue-dependency chain (3.1 done), this is the high-priority win: ships <1s dashboard load at 1k records.
analysis.change_surface: 1 file (App.jsx) for the lazy wiring, plus a tiny Loading fallback component (could be inline in App.jsx, or a new tiny file). No backend / DB / lib changes. The verify command in the issue is `rg -n "from 'd3'|from 'leaflet'|html2canvas" src/dashboard/App.jsx` exits 1 — currently fails because App.jsx has none of these, so the verify already passes; the acceptance criterion is essentially that the static imports are gone from App.jsx (they already are) AND that the four view components are React.lazy()-imported instead of statically imported (this is the new work).
analysis.root_cause: App.jsx eagerly imports the four visualization components at module top, so d3, leaflet, and html2canvas are part of the initial bundle. Splitting them behind React.lazy() defers those imports until the user actually opens graph/bipartite/map/table.

options.name: React.lazy the four view components with one shared Suspense
options.summary: Replace the four static imports in App.jsx with React.lazy(() => import('./components/RadialGraph.jsx')) etc. Wrap the view section in a single <Suspense fallback={<ViewFallback/>}>. Define the fallback inline (small spinner reusing the existing .loading-spinner style from App.css).
pros: Single Suspense boundary keeps layout stable
cons: All four view chunks share the same fallback, but the active-view transition is only one chunk at a time
options.risk_details: React.lazy is well-supported under React 19. The verify command stays the same; the only behavior change is a brief Suspense spinner the first time the user opens a view.

options.name: React.lazy with per-view Suspense fallback
options.summary: Each conditional render (`{activeView === 'graph' && (...)}`) is wrapped in its own Suspense with a view-specific skeleton.
pros: More granular fallbacks, no flicker when switching views
cons: Per-view skeletons are pure duplication since each view is only one at a time
options.risk_details: Slight complexity bump; same verify command.

options_considered: React.lazy the four view components with one shared Suspense
options_rejected: React.lazy with per-view Suspense fallback (Option 2) — single Suspense is sufficient because only one view is mounted at a time
